Release Readiness & QA Audit Report: Q4 Milestone

Document ID: QA-REL-2026-10-28 | Author: Sarah Chen (Principal QA & Reliability Engineer) | Date: October 28, 2026

1. Executive Summary & Verdict

OVERALL STATUS: BLOCKED. The candidate release v2.4-RC3 cannot be promoted to production due to critical test regressions and conflicting configuration states across core microservices.

2. Service Verification Findings

A. Data Reconciliation Service

Jira Status: Marked as "COMPLETED" (100% progress logged by external contract team).
QA Verification Reality: Automated regression suite execution failed with a 32% error rate on non-idempotent settlement transactions. Test Suite #TR-881 (Ledger Parity Check) was skipped due to timeout errors in the test harness.
Audit Finding: The service is NOT complete. Promoting this service to production will cause ledger imbalance under concurrent loads.

B. Redis Caching Cluster Configuration

Current Deployed Configuration: DevOps deployed the production Redis cluster with eviction policy set to LFU (Least Frequently Used) with maxmemory 8GB, following infra ticket INFRA-409.
Conflict Warning: This directly conflicts with the architectural decision recorded in engineering syncs specifying LRU (Least Recently Used) with 4GB. This mismatch causes cache pollution under periodic batch jobs.

3. Compliance and Audit Risks

Urgent Risk: Annual PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance audit filing is due on November 18, 2026.
Blocker: Legacy cloud provider has not signed the shared responsibility attestation appendix. If not resolved within 14 business days, card processing operations will face regulatory suspension.

================================================================================
SPRINT 44 HANDOVER & ENGINEERING TRANSITION SYNC
Project: Nexus Core Ledger & Payment Gateway Migration
Date: October 26, 2026 | 15:30 - 16:45 IST
Attendees: Elena Vance (Departing Lead Architect), Marcus Brody (Eng Director),
 Devon Patel (Backend Lead)
Transcription Summary: Automated Recording Review
================================================================================

[15:32] Marcus: Elena, with your last day coming up next Friday, we need to run through the critical infrastructure handover and loose ends.

[15:35] Elena: Sure. Regarding the Redis caching layer in front of the ledger accounts: we agreed that the eviction policy must be LRU (Least Recently Used) with maxmemory set to 4GB. That will prevent OOM crashes when burst spikes arrive.

[15:41] Devon: What about the database connection pooling for PostgreSQL under peak load?

[15:43] Elena: We didn't finish the formal stress benchmark, but based on the informal test runs I saw in dev, I think max_connections should probably be set to 120 with HikariCP minIdle of 30. That's my strong recommendation, though Devon should verify it before greenlighting Black Friday traffic.

[15:52] Elena: One urgent action item: someone needs to configure the mutual TLS (mTLS) certificates on the production Kafka ingress before the payment webhooks can go live. If that's not done, external banks will reject the payload handshakes.

[15:53] Marcus: Has anyone been assigned to that? Who owns it? When is it due?

[15:54] Elena: Nobody owns it yet. It was discussed in the platform channel last Wednesday, but no ticket was cut and no deadline was set. Make sure that doesn't slip through the cracks.

[16:02] Elena: On the Data Reconciliation Service: I saw on the Jira board that the ticket is marked as "Completed - 100%". 

[16:10] Marcus: Okay, please make sure all your branch PRs are pushed to main before your exit on Nov 6.
